outcome: Response terms, access and declaration authority are agreed before an incident, so containment can start in hours rather than days.
overview: Nobody buys incident response capability during an incident at a sensible price, and the first hours of a serious breach are spent on contracting rather than containment. A Unit 42 retainer converts that into a pre-agreed engagement with defined response times, and the preparation work that comes with it — reviewing what telemetry exists, agreeing who declares an incident — is usually worth more than the retained hours. This record is a service rather than a product, and the honest measure is whether an exercise reaches containment, not whether a contract exists.

benefits.text: Response capability is contracted before it is needed, not during an incident
benefits.limits: A retainer guarantees engagement terms, not an outcome; response quality still depends on the telemetry the estate retained beforehand

benefits.text: Preparation work surfaces the telemetry and decision gaps that would slow a real response
benefits.limits: The findings only help if they are acted on; a readiness review filed and forgotten changes nothing

benefits.text: Unused retainer hours can generally be applied to proactive work rather than lapsing
benefits.limits: Conversion terms vary by contract and must be confirmed in the agreement rather than assumed from this record

residency: Responder access to customer systems is scoped in the engagement terms; where forensic data may not leave the country that constraint is agreed in the retainer rather than negotiated during an incident

notFor.situation: An organisation with an existing incident response retainer
notFor.why: Two retainers create ambiguity about who leads, which is the last thing an incident needs

notFor.situation: An estate with no security telemetry retained
notFor.why: Responders reconstruct from evidence, and where none was kept the retainer buys expertise with nothing to examine

scope:
Model: Vendor-delivered response service with Redington holding the commercial relationship and coordinating the readiness and gap-closure work · Duration: 4–6 weeks to a signed retainer with the readiness review complete; exercise scheduled within the term
Support model: Contracted response times per retainer tier, invoked through the named declaration authority; Redington coordinates the commercial relationship and the preparation programme.
1) Agree — retainer tier, responder access scope, data-handling and residency terms
2) Prepare — readiness review of telemetry, retention and decision authority
3) Name — declaration authority appointed with an out-of-hours path and tested contact route
4) Exercise — tabletop or technical exercise with time to containment measured and findings recorded
deliverables: The declaration route is tested outside working hours and reaches a responder within the contracted time
The readiness review states what telemetry exists, for how long, and what a responder would therefore be unable to examine
Every readiness finding has an owner and a date
effort: 4–6 weeks to a signed retainer with the readiness review complete; exercise scheduled within the term
languages: English delivery; Arabic executive briefing on request
